authority_order: current explicit teacher instruction for the specific job
current Algebra Framework front door plus the current Framework amendment, this authority contract, and declared current course policy files
exact embedded Unit Assessment Plan for exact Learning Targets, I Can statements, Intro/Review/Mastery placement, Mastery Goal identity, and Unit scope
current executable task PM for procedure
assessment_plan_rule: Exact Unit Assessment Plan HTML remains authority for Unit learning content: section titles, Learning Targets, I Can statements, Intro/Review/Mastery placement, Mastery Goal identity/text, representations, misconceptions, and Unit scope. Coursewide recurring-assessment mechanics, Portfolio status language, rollup rules, and just-in-time reassessment routing are delegated to the current Algebra Framework policy files named below. Legacy Exit Ticket/Portfolio wording embedded in older Assessment Plan HTML does not override those current coursewide mechanics.
canonical_goal_identity: When the same goal moves Review -> Mastery, keep the exact goal ID/title/description. Stage changes support/evidence demand, not goal identity.
spiral_rule: Intro Unit N -> Review Unit N+1 -> Mastery Unit N+2; Review Unit N -> Mastery Unit N+1. Section numbers do not need to match across Units.
warmup_rule: Algebra Warm-Ups use a separate four-slot course-long fluency track: Solve / Diamond / Skill Review / Challenge. Do not route daily slots mechanically from Intro/Review/Mastery.
quick_check_rule: Quick Check is the current common short-evidence artifact. Curriculum defines predictable evidence slots; live Portfolio state selects just-in-time reassessment targets; the teacher approves the actual questions. Do not freeze future reassessment I Cans months ahead.
portfolio_status_rule: I Can status uses No Evidence / Developing / Mastered / Transfer. Algebra Mastery Goal is demonstrated when at least 2 of its 4 I Cans are Mastered or Transfer. Unit status uses I/C/B/A/A+ under the current policy contract.
independence_rule: An I Can normally reaches Mastered from at least two independent convincing demonstrations, normally from different opportunities and with at least one reasonably current demonstration. A rich artifact may suffice when it contains multiple genuinely independent demonstrations. Teacher judgment resolves mixed or unusual cases.
bank_rule: The canonical Algebra Bank is reusable question-family architecture organized Mastery Goal -> I Can -> materially different families. It supports fresh downstream authoring; it does not freeze future Quick Check reassessment targets.
derivative_index_rule: If a derivative JSON/index conflicts with exact Assessment Plan learning content, use the Assessment Plan for learning content and regenerate the derivative. If a legacy recurring-assessment derivative conflicts with the current Portfolio/Quick Check policy, use the current policy and quick_check_slot_map.
task_pm_rule: Task PM owns execution procedure and packaging. Framework owns Algebra-specific learning/evidence/resource behavior. PMs may not revive retired Exit Ticket mechanics or retired Portfolio labels.
operational_map_rule: Current delegated operational maps are curriculum/quick_check_slot_map.json for Quick Check slot architecture and curriculum/warmup_progression_map.json for Warm-Up fluency progression. curriculum/exit_evidence_map.* is retired compatibility metadata only.
question_structure_rule: Use current universal Question Structure for authored questions across Bank/downstream resources unless an explicit course rule exempts the resource. Algebra Warm-Ups are the explicit exception. Structure ID, reasoning architecture, student action, response mode, representation, and executable route must agree semantically; metadata-only alignment is not sufficient.
